@graph.description: Discover the LEO Section at Rajadamnern Stadium. See Section 10, the front-facing ring view, seating style, betting nights and booking information.

mainEntity.name: What is the LEO Section at Rajadamnern Stadium?

acceptedAnswer.text: The LEO Section is Section 10, an elevated section facing the front of the ring at Rajadamnern Stadium.

mainEntity.name: Is LEO Section the same as Section 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. LEO Section is Section 10 at Rajadamnern Stadium.

No. LEO seating is unassigned, which means guests choose their position within the section.

Every ticket guarantees a seat.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to stand in LEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There are no standing areas at Rajadamnern Stadium. Every LEO ticket guarantees a seat.

LEO is where the local betting crowd gathers on Wednesday New Power, Thursday Petchyindee and Sunday Kiatpetch.

This atmosphere does not apply to every night of the week.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to take part in betting?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Guests do not have to take part in betting. You can sit alongside the activity, watch what is happening and experience the atmosphere around it.
Visitors may be able to bet, but it should not be described as a simple turn-up-and-bet process. There is a learning curve and established relationships with bookmakers involved.

mainEntity.name: What view do you get from LEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: LEO directly faces the front of the ring and provides a strong view across the whole canvas.

mainEntity.name: Which rows are best in LEO?

acceptedAnswer.text:
MuayTix generally recommends around Row D and above for the clearest overall sightline.

Arriving early gives you more choice of position, but it is not required to secure a seat.

Yes. There is no age restriction preventing children from sitting in LEO.

Club Class is normally the calmer and more straightforward family choice, but LEO can suit families who prefer the atmosphere and seating style.

mainEntity.name: Is LEO the same level as Club Class?

acceptedAnswer.text:
LEO has effectively the same tier, elevation and row configuration as Club Class next door.

The main differences are the concrete tier seating and the unassigned seating arrangement.
It can be. Families who prefer a numbered seat and simpler arrival may find Club Class more straightforward. Families who want the LEO atmosphere can choose LEO.

mainEntity.name: Is there a dress code for LEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no formal smart-casual dress requirement. Dress sensibly for a sporting event inside an air-conditioned arena.
